column2: A measure of frequency stability over different averaging times, used for clocks and oscillators. Its shape reveals which kinds of noise dominate at each timescale.
Measurement techniques that avoid disturbing the quantity being measured, by pushing the unavoidable disturbance into another variable that is not measured.
The lowest possible variance of an unbiased estimator, set by the Fisher information of the data. It limits how precisely a parameter can be measured.
The disturbance a measurement causes to the system being measured, as required by quantum mechanics. It sets fundamental limits on precision sensing.
The ultimate limit on how precisely a parameter can be estimated from a quantum state, set by the quantum Fisher information and optimized over all measurements.
A measure of how sensitively a quantum state changes with a parameter. Higher values mean the parameter can be estimated more precisely.
The smallest change in a signal that a sensor can detect in a given measurement time, often quoted per square root of hertz.
column3: In statistics, sensitivity is a test's true positive rate; in everyday English it means being easily affected.

column2: The precision limit set by counting random particles, such as photons, with error falling as 1/√N. It is the standard quantum limit for optical measurements.
An instrument that splits atoms' matter waves along two paths and recombines them, measuring accelerations, rotations or gravity from the phase difference.
A clock that keeps time by locking to the frequency of an atomic transition, such as in caesium. Atomic clocks define the second and enable GPS.
A gravity sensor that uses atom interferometry with laser-cooled atoms in free fall to measure local gravity very precisely, for geology or navigation.
An imaging technique that forms a picture using correlations between two light beams, one of which never touches the object. It was first shown with entangled photons.
Measuring magnetic fields with nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond, whose spin energy levels shift with the field and can be read optically, even at room temperature.
An atomic clock that uses an optical transition in ions or neutral atoms, ticking far faster than microwave clocks. Optical clocks are the most accurate timekeepers ever built.
A magnetometer that uses laser light to polarize atomic spins, often in alkali vapour, and detects how a magnetic field changes their precession. It can sense brain signals without cryogenics.
A rotation sensor based on quantum effects, such as atom interferometry or spins, for navigation without GPS.
A sensing scheme that uses entangled light to detect a faint object in bright background noise better than any classical light of the same power.
Imaging techniques that use quantum properties of light, such as entanglement or squeezing, to beat classical limits on resolution, noise or light dose.
A magnetic field sensor based on quantum effects, such as SQUIDs, NV centres or atomic vapours, capable of extreme sensitivity.
Feeding squeezed light into an interferometer to lower quantum noise below the shot-noise limit. It is used in gravitational-wave detectors such as LIGO.
A magnetometer built from a superconducting quantum interference device, among the most sensitive magnetic sensors known, used in medicine and materials research.
Using entanglement between sensors at different locations to estimate a combined quantity, such as an average field, more precisely than independent sensors could.
Using entangled probes to measure a quantity with better precision than the standard quantum limit allows for independent particles.
A measurement that leaves the measured quantity unchanged, so repeating it gives the same result. It is used to read out qubits and to count photons without absorbing them.
A precision technique that applies two π/2 pulses separated by free evolution; the phase gained in between reveals frequency differences. It is used in atomic clocks and qubit calibration.
Entangling many spins so that the uncertainty in one direction drops below the standard quantum limit. It improves atomic clocks and magnetometers.
